text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange on Monday closed 0.26 percent down, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 433.23 points, down from 434.37 points on Friday.
ONA, Morocco's largest private conglomerate which has stakes in more than 100 firms, lost 10 dirhams to close at 480 dirhams.
The group has a market capitalisation of 8.4 billion dirhams, stockbrokers said.
"The bourse index drop was considered as a temporary fluctuation...It is expected to resume its upward trend," a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the market's most liquid stocks, lost four dirhams to at 391 dirhams.
Wafabank, was traded at 530 dirhams, similar to last Friday.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate closed at 557, down one.
SNI has diversified stakes in more than 40 companies.
Traded volume on the official market was 18.6 million dirhams compared with 38.8 million dirhams on Friday.
